engine.title: Stop buying strength that has already run
engine.body: The 4H RSI ceiling for longs was 75. Splitting every closed trade by the RSI recorded at entry showed the engine bleeding above 65 and profitable below it. The ceiling is now 65.
engine.note: Holds in both halves of the sample and at every cut point tested (60, 65, 70), so it is not one lucky threshold. The threshold was still chosen from this sample, so treat the size as an upper bound.

engine.title: A break-even stop would not have helped
engine.body: The median losing trade was +1.44R in profit before it reversed, and 59% touched a full +1R first. That looks like an obvious fix: move the stop to entry once price pays 1R. Re-walking every trade bar by bar, with winners subject to the same rule, says otherwise.
engine.note: The first version of this test only altered losers, which guarantees a positive answer. Correcting it reversed the conclusion. Nothing tested cleared one standard error, so no stop rule was adopted.

engine.title: Trades were being closed at prices that never traded
engine.body: The grader had never resolved a single trade — an exception was being swallowed silently — leaving a fallback path that could book an exit at a bar from before the signal existed. Every closed trade was re-graded against bars that actually printed.
evidence: exits corrected to a real price
engine.note: This moved the headline number against me. It is published anyway, because the earlier number was not real. Pre-correction data is kept in the repo rather than deleted.

engine.title: A first target must pay back the risk
engine.body: T1 was whichever structural level sat nearest the entry, with no distance test. One signal shipped a T1 worth 0.19R against its own stop, printed beside an R:R of 2.41 quoted off T2. T1 must now return at least 1R.

chess.title: Tactics: The Skewer
chess.body: A skewer is a reverse pin. A valuable piece is attacked, it moves, and the piece behind it is captured. Skewers happen on open files and diagonals. Rooks and bishops execute skewers. Pattern: Rook checks king → king moves → rook captures queen. Spot this on every open file.

wisdom.title: Joy is a Practise
wisdom.body: Joy doesn't arrive when the conditions are right. It's practiced in the conditions you have. Find one thing today that is genuinely good. Savour it for 30 seconds. This is not toxic positivity — it's neurological training. Brains that practise noticing goodness get better at finding it, even in hard seasons.

book.author: Cal Newport
book.chapter: The Shallow Work Trap: Why Being Busy Is Not the Same as Being Productive
book.lesson: Shallow work is non-cognitively demanding tasks performed while distracted — email, meetings, admin. Deep work is professional activity performed in a state of distraction-free concentration that pushes your cognitive capabilities to their limit. These efforts create new value, improve your skill, and are hard to replicate. Newport's argument: the ability to do deep work is becoming increasingly rare at exactly the same time it is becoming increasingly valuable in the economy. The few who cultivate this skill will thrive.
book.key_quote: Two to four hours of genuine deep work produces more output than eight hours of fragmented shallow work.
book.action: Schedule one 90-minute deep work block tomorrow. No phone, no email, one hard problem. Treat it like a meeting you cannot cancel.
crux: Deep work: focused, undistracted, cognitively demanding work. It is becoming rare and simultaneously more valuable.
Two core abilities now decide income: learn hard things fast, and produce elite output fast.
Both abilities depend on deep work. Both are destroyed by fragmented attention.
Shallow work is logistically necessary and infinitely replaceable. It feels like work and produces nothing durable.
Attention residue: switching tasks leaves cognitive drag for 15–20 minutes. Ten switches cost you the day.
High-quality work = time spent × intensity of focus. Intensity is the neglected multiplier.
Four scheduling philosophies: monastic, bimodal, rhythmic, journalistic. Rhythmic — same hours daily — is the only one most people can sustain.
Willpower is finite and depletes. Rituals and fixed locations spend none of it.
Schedule every minute of the workday. Not to obey it, but to force the question 'what deserves this hour?'
Fixed-schedule productivity: hard-stop the day and work backwards. Constraint forces ruthless triage.
Boredom tolerance is trainable and prerequisite. If every queue is filled with a phone, focus never develops.
Quit social media by default; readmit a tool only if it clearly serves a core goal.
Drain the shallows. Aim shallow work under 40% of the week and defend the rest.
learnings: Busy is not a proxy for valuable. It is usually a proxy for unfocused.
The ability to concentrate is a skill you build, not a mood you catch.
Fragmented time is not additive — four 30-minute blocks are worth far less than one 2-hour block.
Downtime is not idleness; unconscious processing needs it.
examples: Carl Jung built a stone tower at Bollingen and wrote there in the mornings, uninterrupted, while running a clinical practice.
Adam Grant compressed teaching into one semester and batched research into the other — becoming one of the most published psychologists of his generation.
Newport wrote a book, earned a PhD, and published peer-reviewed papers while rarely working past 5:30pm, by hard-stopping his day.
adapt: One 90-minute block before 8am for the highest-leverage build. Phone in another room, not face-down on the desk.
Batch Telegram, Instagram, and email into two windows. Notifications off outside them.
Financial models are deep work. Do them before the market opens, never in gaps between messages.
Hard-stop at 7pm on weekdays. The constraint is what forces the triage.

minimalism.title: Say No To Free
minimalism.body: Free samples, conference tote bags, hotel toiletries. Free acquisitions carry the same ongoing cost as bought ones. The price tag was never the expensive part.
minimalism.action: Decline the next free item you are offered.
minimalism.label: Minimalism

etiquette.title: Accept The Coffee
etiquette.body: In Gulf business culture, refusing offered coffee or dates can read as refusing the relationship. Take it, hold it, sip it. The transaction is not the point of the meeting.
etiquette.action: Accept the next hospitality offered, even if you do not want it.
etiquette.label: Etiquette

stillness.title: Sit For Ten Minutes
stillness.body: Not to achieve anything. Sit, breathe, and let thoughts pass without following them. The mind wandering is not failure — noticing it wandered is the entire rep.
stillness.action: Ten minutes. Timer on. No app required.
stillness.label: Stillness

model.title: Loss Aversion
model.body: Losses hurt roughly twice as much as equivalent gains please. This makes you hold losing positions and sell winners — precisely backwards, and reliably so.
model.action: Review one holding you are keeping only because selling would confirm the loss.
model.label: Mental Model

arabic.use: Emphasis. 'Wallah?' means 'seriously?'. Extremely common; use lightly.
arabic.label: Arabic

drill.title: Estimate Before Calculating
drill.body: Guess the answer before opening the spreadsheet. Then compare. This builds the instinct that catches a model error before the client does.
drill.action: Estimate three figures before computing. Track how close you were.
drill.label: Drill

health.title: Blood Panel Annually, Minimum
health.body: ApoB, HbA1c, fasting insulin, hs-CRP, lipid panel, vitamin D. ApoB predicts cardiovascular risk better than LDL-C and is rarely ordered unless you ask specifically.
health.action: Book the panel. Ask for ApoB by name.
health.label: Health

quote.name: Michael Bloomberg
quote.quote: In business, what's dangerous is not to evolve.

lesson.lesson: A year from now, you will wish you had started today.

case.title: Slack: From Failed Game to $27B
case.story: Slack's founders built a failed multiplayer game called Glitch. They salvaged the internal communication tool they'd built. Sold to Salesforce for $27B.
case.lesson: Pivots are not failures — they're redirected learning. The most valuable thing from a failed product is often the tool you built to build it.

fpna.title: Sensitivity Tables
fpna.body: Use Excel's Data Table (What-If Analysis) to show EBITDA across assumptions. One table > 5 slides.

cfo.title: FC Step 4: ERP Ownership
cfo.body: SAP S/4HANA or Oracle Fusion — the FC owns the finance module. Know chart of accounts design, cost centre structure, intercompany eliminations, period-end close in the system. This separates candidates. SAP certification: ₹15K online.

money_hack.title: Credit Card Strategy
money_hack.body: Use card for all spends, pay in full before due. Earn 1–2% cashback. Never pay interest.

dubai.title: Consolidation is the differentiator
dubai.body: Multi-entity, multi-currency consolidation with intercompany elimination is what a Gulf group does every month and what most candidates have never touched. Naming the tool — HFM, OneStream, Tagetik, SAP BPC — moves you up a band on its own.
dubai.targets: IFRS 10, IFRS 3 and IAS 21 are the standards behind it. Know which does what.
dubai.action: Take one 20-entity consolidation end to end, even as an exercise. Then say so.

desk.productivity: Shutdown ritual: write tomorrow's top 3, close all tabs. Stop working.

father.title: Read her a real book
father.do: Read something you are reading, aloud, for five minutes. Content is irrelevant.
father.why: Prosody, turn-taking and attention are carried by adult speech regardless of vocabulary. It also means reading time survives on days when the board pack is due.

father.title: Let her see you fail
father.do: When you drop or fumble something in front of her, react calmly and try again visibly.
father.why: Emotional regulation is learned by observation long before instruction. Your reaction to small frustrations is a template she is already recording.

life_wisdom.teaching: Jain tradition treats harsh speech as a form of violence, listing it alongside physical harm rather than as a lesser category.
life_wisdom.apply: Review one message you sent under pressure this week. Would you send it unchanged now? The gap between those two versions is the practice.

life_wisdom.teaching: Something can be true conventionally and empty ultimately — a table is a table for practical purposes and a collection of parts on analysis. Both are needed.
life_wisdom.apply: Hold the forecast as both real enough to act on and provisional enough to abandon. Treating a model as ultimately true is how people ride a position down.

speaking.title: Say the difficult number
speaking.drill: Practise delivering bad news out loud: 'We are AED 14M behind.' No preamble, no cushion.
speaking.why: The instinct is to soften it with context first. Context after the number is briefing; before it is stalling.

interview_tech.q: Your CEO wants to grow revenue 20%. Finance says cash cannot fund it. How do you frame that?
interview_tech.a: Not as a refusal. Compute the sustainable growth rate: ROE × retention ratio. If the business sustainably funds 12% and the ask is 20%, the gap is 8 points that must come from somewhere — debt, equity, working capital release, or margin. Present the three routes with the cost of each and the covenant headroom. Then let the CEO choose. Finance's job is to price the options, not to be the department that says no.

interview_tech.q: Same-store sales are flat but the store is more profitable. Is that good?
interview_tech.a: Depends entirely on the cause. If margin rose from better buying, less markdown, or labour-scheduling efficiency — excellent, that is real operating leverage. If it rose because you cut staff hours below service thresholds, deferred maintenance, or stopped local marketing, you are harvesting the store and flat sales will turn negative within three quarters. Ask for the conversion rate and units per transaction, not just the margin.

interview_soft.q: What questions do you have for us?
interview_soft.a: Never none. Ask things that reveal you are evaluating them: what does the first 12 months look like for whoever takes this; what is the finance function currently not able to answer that the board keeps asking; how is the relationship between finance and the commercial teams today; and why is the role open. The last one is the most informative and the least asked. Avoid salary and benefits at first interview.

interview_soft.q: Describe a situation where you had incomplete information and had to decide anyway.
interview_soft.a: Forecasting and provisioning are full of these. Structure: what you knew, what you could not know in the time available, the cost of waiting, the assumption you took and why, and how you made the assumption visible rather than burying it. The mark of seniority is deciding with 70% of the information and saying explicitly what would change your mind — say that phrase.
